newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks edge down as prices settle.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks edge down as prices settle.

text.p: Colombian stocks edged down Thursday amid profit-taking following recent meteoric rises that transformed the country's markets into some of the world's best performers this year.

Bogota's IBB index fell back 0.49 percent to 1,033.41 on a 4.1 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index drifted down 0.08 percent to 16,406.27 on 4.6 billion pesos. "The fall in bank prices continued and some manufacturing and retail companies also began to drop. The price correction could continue Friday, although many foreign funds are looking for shares," said one Bogota broker.
Medellin market analyst Stephen Edkins forecast indices could drop back between five and 10 percent before rising again at the start of the second quarter.

Year-on-year, he forecast both Bogota and Medellin would produce nominal returns of between 40 percent and 45 percent. Taking into account the latest price corrections, both markets are still up about 22 percent in the year so far after three years of virtual stagnation.
The biggest fallers in Bogota were Banco Ganadero ordinary shares, down 2.29 percent to 298, and Banco Industrial Colombiano, down 2.01 percent to 3,900.
"These falls are normal after the speculative wave that began Friday and continued through this week. A mix of foreign funds and local investors were selling," said a Bogota broker.

Insurance company Suramericana fell 1.45 percent to 21,710 and supermarket chain Carulla lost 1.44 percent to close at 5,600 -- which brokers said could have been due to the government announcement of a new tax on debit card purchases.
The biggest losers in Medellin were supermarket chain Cadenalco, down 5 percent to 950, Bancoquia, down 4.08 percent to 2,820 and cement maufacturer Cementos Caribe, down 3.03 percent at 5,600.
The fall was offset by an 18.9 percent leap in food manufacturer Industrias Alimenticias Noel, which closed at 3,510, and timber merchants Tablemac, up 9.25 percent to 37.44.
